title: Visual Information Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DIR COMM
raw_text:
2.     MOS 4503, Visual Information Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DIR COMM

    a. Summary. The Visual Information Officer (VIO) is a highly skilled
technical expert in the 45XX occupational field, specializing in the
application of organic visual information capabilities. Serving as the
principal advisor to commanders and Communication Strategy and Operations
(COMMSTRAT) Officers, the VIO provides expertise on all visual information
matters. Their responsibilities include enhancing the proficiency and
effectiveness of personnel by mentoring and training officers and Marines in
mechanical, doctrinal, and conceptual aspects of visual information. VIOs
play a critical role in developing training, exercises, and operational plans
that support mission-essential tasks, meet communication objectives, and
ensure compliance with individual and collective training and readiness
standards. They manage visual information equipment and commodities within
their unit, ensuring operational readiness, and they regularly report on the
unit’s technical proficiency. VIOs have a comprehensive understanding of
DOTMLPF-C (doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership and
education, personnel, facilities, and cost) from a program management
perspective. They are responsible for requirements management, including
forecasting and analyzing financial data to support informed decisions.
Additionally, VIOs oversee indoctrination and certification programs, develop
annexes and appendices to operational orders, integrate emerging
technologies, review training and readiness manuals, and participate in
advisory groups and trade shows. They may also serve as Combat Camera
(COMCAM) planners, tasked with planning, sustaining, and employing COMCAM
capabilities across various operational environments. In this capacity, they
work closely with numbered fleets, joint force commands (JFCs), and
Headquarters Marine Corps (HQMC) to ensure the readiness of personnel and the
successful execution of COMCAM operations.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must have a GT score of 110 or higher.

            (2) Must hold PMOS 4591 with minimum of three-year experience as a
4591.




                                        1-213                          Enclosure (1)
 1128                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Must possess a school-trained 45XX (or legacy 43XX or 46XX)
background.

        (4) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

        (5) Security requirement: must possess secret security clearance;
must meet sensitive compartmented information (SCI) eligibility guidelines
based on a single scope background investigation/T5 investigation.

        (6) Must have graduated from at least one visual information
management course. Eligible courses are limited to the Visual Information
Management Course (A18M6N2) or the Combat Camera Leadership Course (A18A412)
both at DINFOS, Ft Meade, MD.

        (7) Must have graduated from at least one visual information
technical course. Eligible courses are limited to the Digital Multimedia
Course (A18T4Z2), Intermediate Photojournalism Course (A1843E2), Intermediate
Motion Media/Intermediate Videography Course (A18KCU2), Advanced Electronic
Journalism Course (A18PNL2) all at DINFOS, Ft Meade, MD, the Department of
Defense-Sponsored Military Photojournalism (MPJ) Course (C244661), or the
Military Motion Media (MMM) Course (C2446P1), Military Visual Journalism
Program at S.I. Newhouse School of Public Communications at Syracuse
University.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC)
(M02RMN4) within 18 months of appointment to WO.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to the
Communication Strategy and Operations Training and Readiness Manual (NAVMC
3500.9C).

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) General and Operations Managers 11-1021.

            (2) Marketing Managers 11-2021.

            (3) Training and Development Managers 11-3131.

            (4) Project Management Specialists 13-1082.

            (5) Training and Development Specialists 13-1151.

            (6) Archivists 25-4011.

            (7) Art Directors 27-1011.

            (8) Graphic Designers 27-1024.

            (9) Set and Exhibit Designers 27-1027.

            (10) Producers and Directors 27-2012.

            (11) Writers and Editors 27-3040.

            (12) Broadcast, Sound, and Lighting Technicians 27-4010.




                                         1-214                         Enclosure (1)
 1128                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



            (13) Photographers 27-4021.

            (14) Television, Video, and Film Camera Operators and Editors 27-
4030.

            (15) Media and Communication Equipment Workers, All Other 27-4099.

            (16) Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks 43-5061.

            (17) Audiovisual Equipment Installers and Repairers 49-2097.

            (18) Printing Workers 51-5110.

            (19) Photographic Process Workers and Processing Machine Operator 51-
9150.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Combat Camera Officer, 4602.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
